info.title: Taskless CLI API
info.description: Internal API consumed by the Taskless CLI.

bearerAuth.description: JWT issued via device authorization flow (POST /cli/auth/token). Claims: sub (Taskless user UUID), iss ("cli"), exp, orgId (GitHub org numeric ID). The orgId claim identifies the billing organization for this token.

get.summary: Returns authenticated user identity and organizations

url.description: Canonical owner URL the client matches its repository against

prompt.description: Description of the rule to generate

successCases.description: Examples of correct code that should pass the rule (optional)

failureCases.description: Examples of incorrect code that should fail the rule (optional)

requestId.description: UUID of the generation request (the ticket the rules are generated under)

ruleId.description: Deprecated: use requestId. Same value — this identifies the generation request, not a rule

get.summary: Get generation request status and output (poll until terminal state)

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: UUID of the generation request. One request produces N rules, each with its own `id`.

requestId.description: UUID of the generation request the rules were generated under

rules.description: Generated rules (present when status is generated). Clients below the `file-set` floor receive `content`; clients at or above it receive `files`.

rule.description: Rule object to find matching AST nodes

message.description: Message explaining why the rule fired

note.description: Additional notes to elaborate the message

files.description: Glob patterns the rule applies to

valid.description: Code that should NOT trigger the rule

invalid.description: Code that SHOULD trigger the rule

files.description: Every file the rule directory must contain

signature.description: Blessed canonical signature, when one was registered

files.description: Every file the rule directory must contain

signature.description: Blessed canonical signature, when one was registered

files.description: Every file the rule directory must contain

engine.description: Executable — check.ts runs against a file tree

signature.description: REQUIRED. Execution is gated on this signature, so a runtime rule without one could never run.

items.description: A rule directory as files, relative to .taskless/rules/

meta.description: Sidecar metadata keyed by rule filename (present when rules are present)

requestId.description: UUID of the generation request that produced this rule

installationId.description: GitHub App installation ID (absent for public repos)

error.description: Why the request ended the way it did. Present when status is `failed` (a generation error) or `unsupported` (the request was understood and refused — for example an engine this client version cannot receive). A client SHOULD surface this text rather than substituting its own, since it names what the user must do.

errorCode.description: Machine-readable companion to `error`, so a client can branch on a specific outcome instead of matching prose. `ENGINE_NOT_DELIVERABLE` means the rule needed an engine this client version cannot receive and the fix is a CLI upgrade.

parameters.description: UUID of the generation request. One request produces N rules, each with its own `id`.

guidance.description: Feedback for iterating on the existing rule
